number.why: The served HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.64–1.80) matches recurrent symptomatic VTE and VTE-related deaths during six months of acute treatment, comparing dabigatran with warfarin. HR 1.13 belongs to follow-up through the post-treatment period. Agreement retains the ruling's population qualification: this is FAS, requiring at least one dose, rather than unrestricted intention-to-treat.

Full analysis set (FAS): consisted of all randomised patients who were documented to have taken at least one dose of study drug. Patients were assigned to the treatment groups as randomised, i.e. regardless of the actual medication taken.

entry.why: Registry inclusion criteria explicitly establish adults with acute symptomatic proximal DVT and/or PE. The abstract establishes the randomized dabigatran-versus-warfarin comparison following initial heparin treatment.

quotes.span: Inclusion criteria: * Acute symptomatic uni- or bilateral Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) of the leg involving proximal veins, and/or Pulmonary Embolism (PE) * Male or female, being 18 years of age or older

In a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial of 2589 patients with acute VTE treated with low-molecular-weight or unfractionated heparin for 5 to 11 days, we compared dabigatran 150 mg twice daily with warfarin.

missed: No additional finding changes either verdict. The registry eligibility quote supplies explicit adult and symptomatic-entry evidence absent from the ruling's cited population span. The FAS-versus-intention-to-treat discrepancy was already identified and requires accurate population labeling.
